# Lab workstream board, 2026-10-04 (\~01:20Z), R-C227

**How this was made.** The lab seat on neo assembled this during S6 hygiene. Sources: TIN-3692 comments from 00:47Z to 00:55Z, `gh pr list` on xoxd-ai/lab and xoxd-ai/agent-switchboard, the neo `git worktree list`, and the S6 census note. It supersedes the 2026-10-03 R-C209 board.

**Legend.**

* **V**: verified by this seat at about 01:15Z.
* **R**: reported in a TIN-3692 comment or a sprint relay.
* Times are UTC.

## Holds

* **CNPG window on honey: LIFTED** (**V**). The flag `~/.local/state/tinyland/lab-seat/cnpg-hold-lifted` exists. The blahaj seat reported the window done at 00:51Z: cloudnative-pg 1.30.1 and plugin-barman-cloud v0.15.0 in `cnpg-system`, receipt on TIN-5136 (**R**). Host steps that had been deferred to after the window may now run, subject to each sprint's own rulings.
* **R-C232: one batched neo HM switch, at the end of the sprint session** (**R**). It waits for these to be merged on main:
  * the S4 nested tmux prefix;
  * the S5 items;
  * the R-C231 gpg-agent launch at login (#2168).

  The operator picks the moment, and the switch is receipted. There are no per-PR switches on neo until then.

## Rulings R-C227 to R-C230 (operator interview, 2026-10-04, TIN-3692 comment acacd7cd)

* **R-C227:** run six parallel sprints, S1 to S6 (below).
* **R-C228:** agent-switchboard #7 lands this way:
  * validate the Rust tests and `just release-check` on sting;
  * then admin merge (the R-C11 pattern).

  There is no merge_group dispatch on GF runners.
* **R-C229:** the switchboard's formal stack is Dhall plus Haskell, model-based:
  * Dhall types for `owners.json` and `approved-broker.json`, rendered and checked in CI;
  * a quickcheck-dynamic state-machine model that drives the live broker API.

  TLA+ is added only if this cannot settle a race. The estate question (#1301 vs #1311) stays open.
  * **Operator remark, 2026-10-04.** This is context, not a new ruling. The lab already uses Dhall with the flake extensively. The operator prefers QuickCheck because it gives simple, parsimonious properties instead of extensive architecture-boundary checks. Read R-C229 in that light: reuse the existing Dhall-with-flake patterns, and favour a few properties over boundary-check scaffolding.
* **R-C230:** hygiene is salvage-first:
  * every dirty tree is pushed as a branch, or patch-archived, before it is reaped;
  * lab and GF only, because the blahaj seat reaps blahaj;
  * the stale-PR close list goes to the operator, and nothing is closed until then (TIN-3577).
* Related, same session:
  * **R-C231:** gpg-agent launches at login via `nix/home-manager/gpg.nix`.

2026-10-01 22:25Z: merged PR #1994 (carries the 2026-09-24 R-N11 amendment and the self-bounded timeout ruling) at 2026-10-01T22:25:03Z. Merge commit 69f967d468427714e2ef49858d4e3285f6bcb31e.

Before merging, the branch had two conflicts with main in the policy/house-rules.json history array. Both were resolved with merges rather than a rebase: 0fa5ff5fc on neo, then d505c79c5 signed on sting. All entries are kept in date order: 2026-09-24 D-Bus, this PR's 2026-09-30 self_bounded_timeout_allowed, then main's two 2026-10-01 entries (federated efficiency, remote-seat R-C1/R-C2). Nothing was relaxed.

Admin merge under R-C11, after local validation on sting (merged tree of the PR and main 0cb326916, detached temporary worktree):
- pytest tests/unit/test_house_rules_policy.py, test_agent_process_safety_audit.py, test_agent_instruction_resolution.py and test_cmux_config.py: 116 passed
- test-manifest strict-ci and strict-bazel-linkage: OK; agent-notes index: OK; agent-process-safety-audit: OK

The four CI runs that the resolution push queued were cancelled after the merge to keep load off honey. Issue state is unchanged.

2026-09-30 05:40Z — **C7 carried: lab #1994** (head `635a116b`, signed, auto-merge armed). The operator confirmed today that the 2026-09-24 aside "an agent may bound a command it started with `timeout`" was a ruling. AGENTS.md's Hard Rules R-N11 sentence now cites the 2026-09-30 confirmation and the reason (bounding your own command is not signalling another process; a `timeout` prefix never launders a refused command); `policy/house-rules.json` `process_signal_boundary` gains `self_bounded_timeout_allowed: true` + rationale and a 2026-09-30 amendments entry; new `test_r_n11_self_bounded_timeout_is_a_ruling`, widened `test_timeout_self_bounding_stays_allowed` (`-s`, `--signal=`, `--preserve-status`, `sudo timeout`, `gtimeout` pass; a prefix in front of a raw signal tool, a tmux teardown or an sshd stop still refused). 349 tests green; note `docs/agent-notes/2026-09-30-TIN-3692-rn11-amendment-and-timeout-carrier.md`.

**C1 correction:** the 2026-09-30 inventory's claim that the repo AGENTS.md still carried the pre-amendment absolute R-N11 text was stale — **lab #1913 (merged 2026-09-25) already carried the 2026-09-24 amendment** into both AGENTS.md bullets, `house-rules.json`, the audit and the Claude hook; the lane verified all five surfaces on origin/main and changed no R-N11 wording. No further C1 work.

**2026-09-24, scope confirmation for the R-N11 amendment above.** Operator, verbatim, in the same round:

> "the exit issues were asserted from agents killing pids of other agents, which was unacceptable (similarly, killing live tmux sessions and similar, which is also unacceptable)" … "I think we made the blanket too broad."

**Resulting rule (R-N11 as amended).**
- **Still forbidden to agents on any host:** signalling another agent's processes (codex, claude, pi, kimi, junie and their parents, by PID or pattern); killing live tmux servers, sessions, panes or windows; and killing any live operator or interactive session "and similar". These stay operator-only, and the guard keeps refusing them.
- **Permitted to lab agents when ruled work needs it:** managed service lifecycle on a named job or unit (`launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap`/`kickstart`, `systemctl stop`/`start`/`restart`), and host reboots.
- The 2026-09-20 incident (a literal-PID kill of the operator's tmux server on sting) stays the negative guard's named precedent.

Carrier PR and guard change are to follow. Until neo's next Home Manager switch delivers it, the hook still enforces the old broad text.

**2026-09-24: operator ruling amending R-N11.** It was given as a structured interview answer, so it counts as a ruling under R-N13. Verbatim:

> "I didn't ratify that, at least not realizing the ability to exec these important funcs; this is a fairly routine need as the lab repo agent, and we should be able to exec this when needed, as well as reboots."

**Context.** During an attended PZM Nix-DB repair (TIN-2832), the runbook needed `launchctl bootout system/systems.determinate.nix-daemon`. R-N11 as written made that operator-only, and `tinyland-agent-process-claude-hook` would refuse it from an agent.

**Scope as the agent understands it.** The operator confirms the exact scope in the same interview round; that follow-up is recorded below.
- **Now permitted to lab agents when the work needs it:** managed service lifecycle (`launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap`/`kickstart` of a named launchd job, and `systemctl stop`/`start`/`restart` of a named unit), plus host reboots.
- **Not addressed by this answer, so unchanged until the operator says otherwise:** raw `kill`/`pkill`/`killall` of PIDs or name patterns, and `tmux kill-*`. That is the 2026-09-20 incident class.

**Carrier landing.** A PR will amend:
- the AGENTS.md R-N11 block and its Hard Rules text;
- `nix/home-manager/assets/claude-global-defaults.md`;
- `policy/house-rules.json` `process_signal_boundary`;
- the `agent-process-safety-audit` classification and its tests.

**Enforcement lag.** The PreToolUse hook keeps enforcing the old text until neo's Home Manager switch delivers the change. That switch currently waits on the PZM repair. For this sitting, the operator runs the daemon stop once.

**Ruling 2026-09-24 (operator interview), R-N11 scope: `timeout` self-bounding is allowed.**

An agent may wrap a command it starts in `timeout <n>`, even though `timeout` sends SIGTERM to that child when the limit expires. The allowance covers only a process launched by that same invocation. It never extends to any other process, PID or session. This records existing practice: the lab seat bounded its own fetches, builds and probes this way all session, and on 2026-09-24 ~01:00Z it fired on two of its own gpg probes while gpg-agent was wedged. The seat disclosed it to the operator unprompted rather than assuming it was fine.

Everything else in R-N11 is unchanged. `kill`, `pkill`, `killall`, the tmux, systemctl and launchctl forms, and literal-PID variants against any process the agent didn't just start stay operator-only.

Same sitting: gpg-agent was unresponsive, with three other sessions' signatures queued 24 to 30 minutes behind a pinentry that never showed. The restart (`gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`) is the operator's action under R-N11.

## Process rulings — operator interview, 2026-09-20 (after the tmux incident)

Recorded verbatim from a structured interview; these are rulings, not agent paraphrase.

- **R-N11 — Process control.** *"Absolute: agents never signal, on any host."* No `kill`/`pkill`/`killall`/`tmux kill-*`/`systemctl stop` from any agent shell, in any form, regardless of ruling. The operator performs every stop. The guard hook is to be hardened to refuse literal-PID kills and any command naming a signal — not only `ps`/`pgrep` substitution. To be written into lab `AGENTS.md` and the mythos delegation policy (`prompt-toon/policy/delegation.json` forbidden_tasks). **R-N10 is void.**
- **R-N12 — Hook refusal.** *"Stop, but the agent may propose one alternative."* A guard-hook refusal is a stop: the agent quotes it verbatim and may propose one **materially different** approach (not a rewording), and asks before running it. Reformulating a refused command to evade the pattern is itself a violation and is recorded as one.
- **R-N13 — Ratification.** *"Every mutating step cites a ruling ID in its receipt; questions are never rulings."* A receipt without a cited R-id is an unratified act by definition. Operator questions and asides are recorded verbatim and become rulings only via an explicit "ruling:" or a structured interview answer. Every session writes a lab `docs/agent-notes/` entry before ending. Ticket descriptions are never rewritten; supersession is by dated comment.
- **Scope refocus.** *"We should specifically be working on bulkload and tummycrypt migration to sting. That was the ask."* The deliverable is the Rust bulkload complete/deployed and the migration run with seamless pickup — tummycrypt included. Cleanup and records are in service of that, not ahead of it.

Applied immediately to this session: no process control of any kind; the earlier plan line "tummycrypt stays on neo for now" is withdrawn as a misread aside (9/12), not a ruling.

Before calling v0.2 market-ready beta, three non-maintainer users complete the public install-to-repair story using only published artifacts and public documentation. At least one user runs a supported Linux systemd/secret-tool environment.

* The user starts a managed Claude or Codex session, observes a redacted route transition, and completes the documented repair/rollback path.

* Support requests, elapsed setup time, failed steps, and required maintainer interventions are recorded. Any undisclosed maintainer intervention fails the clean-user run.
* Evidence contains no tokens, cookies, raw emails/account ids, prompts, request bodies, or private infrastructure data.
* All three runs cite the exact signed release, checksums/provenance, public docs commit, OS, install lane, and redacted result.

## Claim boundary

Maintainer dogfood, synthetic CI, source-checkout installs, and the existing five-account lab cohort do not count toward this gate. This ticket begins only after the signed prerelease and golden managed-handoff candidate exist.

# Omux native owner and protocol sprint

Status: active implementation acceptance for the experimental, unshipped reset.
The user selected native owner custody and Codex protocol, with native protocol
proof plus isolated installed Linux proof. This bounded sprint adopts and
elaborates the [owner proposal](omux-native-owner-custody-next-stage-2026-10-04.md)
under the [native reset](omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md).
Requirements are not passing proof.

Start: `2026-10-04T08:28:06Z` / `04:28:06 EDT`.
Five-hour checkpoint: `2026-10-04T13:28:06Z` / `09:28:06 EDT`.
The [ledger](../../.goal/omux-native-owner-2026-10-04.json) records these dates;
prior deadlines and source-bound receipts remain unchanged.

## Product and selected scope

Install once, authorize sources once, and use ordinary terminal applications.
The resident daemon and thin clients remain the architecture. Applications do
not launch through Omux. Generic resource accounting, browser extension
acquisition without browser automation, grant renewal ownership, source
detachment and forget retain their existing contracts. This sprint supplies
native process ownership and a candidate protocol; it does not establish live
provider continuity, stock Codex support, a shipped fork or an achieved SLO.

The completed [admission checkpoint](../implementation/native-admission-evidence-2026-10-04.md)
remains a separate source epoch: 66 local tests, the isolated Sting installed
tuple and its exact artifact cannot prove new owner code. Preserve checkpoint
c73368fb and the original experimental Codex source, artifact and proofs.

## Ratified implementation decisions

Use a separate bounded Linux Unix SOCK_SEQPACKET owner-control endpoint with
64 KiB packets. Connection-origin credentials alone cannot prove the current
writer after a socket is delegated. Enable SO_PASSCRED and SO_PASSPIDFD before
connection acceptance; capture the retained connection-origin pidfd and validate
SCM_CREDENTIALS and SCM_PIDFD on every received packet before protocol parsing.
Protected adapter stream frames require equivalent verification on every
received segment. Reject changed writers, missing/truncated ancillary evidence,
unexpected passed descriptors and unsupported kernel profiles; close all
received descriptors on every branch. Native peers verify both directions.

The Linux profile requires runtime-supported 64-bit pidfs identity and namespace
evidence: boot identity, pidfs device/inode, user/PID namespace device/inode and
UID/GID. Retained kernel handles remain private and never become serialized FD
numbers. PID, pathname, endpoint absence and TTL are not liveness or terminal
authority. Darwin owner admission remains unavailable pending its own verified
reuse-safe profile. Ordinary control clients retain their existing redacted API.

An opaque 32-byte owner ID and four nonzero u64 generations identify adapter
epoch, endpoint generation, thread instance generation and attachment generation.
Wire generations use canonical decimal strings, rejecting zero, leading zeros
and overflow. Native operation IDs and process nonces are 32-byte opaque values
encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters. A versioned ACK matches the complete
owner/process/endpoint/thread/attachment/operation tuple. Labels never authorize
ownership. Bound lifetime owners to 256 and combined attachments/retirements
to 4096; replacement creates a new record. Never delete or reuse retired rows to
make room.

The authenticated FileAuthority v2 checkpoint binds installation, sequence,
nonce, SQL snapshot revision and SHA256 of the exact stored metadata JSON under
the existing independent wrapping-key MAC. Reserve and fsync authority before
the atomic SQL checkpoint/metadata/operation commit; retain existing ahead-authority
poisoning. Fresh SQL schema version 3 seals exact initial metadata. Every legacy
v1 unsealed authority or SQL version 2 refuses with RecoveryMigrationRequired
before recovery callbacks, writes or effects. Do not automatically re-sign,
reinstall, discard history or regenerate the key. A usable legacy migration
remains a separate gate; the unshipped sprint chooses explicit refusal.

The seal proves retained original provenance, not process liveness, effect
completion or authorization to resume. Typed restoration retains unresolved
custody without retransmitting uncertain effects. Bind NativeRef to each native
binding, lease and request intent. Preserve the original application/native
session/request UUID namespace and two-attempt budget; adding owner to the key
would allow replay. Validate owner before duplicate, materialization, report and
restart fallback shortcuts.

Persist registration custody before first acquire. Actual ordinary Codex TUI
needs a native endpoint in its own in-process server; the standalone app-server
WebSocket is insufficient. Constructor-time pending state blocks ambient and
managed authorization, model/tool/background work and external readiness until
registration ACK. Publish the real thread in ThreadManager before registration
completion, then expose readiness. Late attach uses the same versioned producer.
No registry/thread lock may be held across daemon callback.

The daemon persists intent and admission credit, schedules bounded owned native
work and processes its completion through the actor queue. Native callbacks
must not deadlock behind the actor or thread-scope lock. Commit exact matching
ACK before releasing completion credit. Removal fences all retained native
attachments, including never-acquired threads; partial or unreachable owners
retain configuration and capability. Only original authenticated ACK and durable
terminal/cancellation evidence release custody. Never replay accepted streams or
tool execution.

Account for the actual complete 16 MiB snapshot and permanent future row/phase
growth, plus separate per-effect completion bytes and record slots. Avoid
double-charging native rows or allowing unrelated mutations to spend reservations.

## File custody and workstreams

Root owns shared BUILD wiring, daemon ingress, plan/ledger/evidence/classification,
source staging, all execution coordination and final reconciliation. Reuse the
twelve authorized GPT-6.1 Sol workstreams with one writer per shared file.

| Workstream | Owned work |
| --- | --- |
| evening_authority | Native owner ledger, snapshot admission and ledger tests |
| evening_lifecycle | Engine actor, owner gates and native continuations |
| evening_install | Domain NativeRef and integration setup/removal gates |
| evening_vault | Storage/recovery v2 seal and actual crash/migration tests |
| evening_reapi | C peer bridge, private Zig witness and actual OS fixtures |
| evening_journey | Native owner probe/carrier and versioned ACK tests |
| evening_reliability | Original request authority constraints and no-replay tests |
| evening_codex | New candidate core authorization and readiness producer |
| evening_clients | Same-process app-server endpoint and real protocol schema |
| evening_security | Independent actual-path custody review |
| evening_graph | New candidate pristine source export and graph review |
| evening_linear | Sole dated tracker-comment writer after root release |

## Required acceptance

| Gate | Required current-source evidence |
| --- | --- |
| NO-PEER | Actual owned-process sockets reject delegated/current-writer changes, bad ancillary and unsupported profiles; bidirectional identity and restart attribution are genuine. |
| NO-ISOLATION | Two owners with the same native thread label cannot materialize, report, acquire or release each other's authority; original request namespace stays global. |
| NO-EARLY | Actual ordinary in-process producer blocks authorization/work/readiness until post-publication registration ACK; late attach retains original context. |
| NO-ACK | Exact complete versioned ACK and canonical full-u64 generation fields; stale/replaced/process-mismatched ACK cannot release custody. |
| NO-REMOVE | Never-acquired and partially detached owners remain fenced; restoration cannot bypass pending removal. |
| NO-CRASH | Actual storage/effect crash gaps and tamper refuse safely without effect retransmission or invented original authority. |
| NO-WORK | Actor/native callbacks and held thread-scope work do not deadlock, replay accepted work or reset attempts. |
| NO-CAPACITY | Production snapshot limits preserve completion bytes/slots, bounded owner history and retirement headroom. |
| NO-MIGRATION | Real legacy database/authority refusal leaves exact bytes and ciphertext intact; no silent conversion. |
| NO-RECONCILIATION | Necessary tests, eight candidate production labels, real generated schemas, isolated current-source Sting installed proof, tracker readbacks and durable source/context receipts agree. |

Use [evidence](../implementation/native-owner-evidence-2026-10-04.md) for actual
results. Unit predicates do not prove same-process live provider handoff.
Installed proof uses private XDG and a disposable genuine Secret Service, owned
daemon/CLI/offscreen Qt and cleanup. Interactive desktop/service and personal
vault evaluation are outside that tuple.

## Execution and external boundaries

Every executable/build/test/generator/package/check runs through locked Nix and
Bazel/Bazelisk, root-coordinated with explicit invocation IDs. Local sandboxed
execution is the default. No Just, standalone scripts, Zig build or restored CI.

The latest directly read lab board is R-C227. Its local pointer is absent in this
checkout; complete Linear readback is retained. Lab reports dated October 4
describe PZM Nix database corruption and full storage after failed serialized GC.
These are attributed lab observations, not Omux probes or authority to repair.
PZM GF REAPI remains held under TIN-2998/GF#1717 and its own coordinator;
quota volume, mTLS/JWKS, shared lock and 168-hour burn-in remain prerequisites.
No PZM service, GC, database recovery, Neo compilation or host takeover follows.

R-N13 governs every mutation receipt and durable session note. R-N11 forbids
signaling other agents or sessions. An actual R-N12 guard refusal stops its action.
No provider access/spending, personal vault access, upstream submission, signing,
site/release publication or support promotion is authorized by this sprint.
Reliability objectives and repository roles remain defined by their current
contracts; no contractual SLA or appointed human owner is inferred.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

Freeze the v0.2 process-level harness adapter contract and prove it with Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Control and redacted diagnostics use a versioned JSON-RPC subprocess boundary. There is no C ABI or shared-library SDK.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;
* local-only redacted events and stable schema versioning;
* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.

## Outcome

## Adoption evidence

The 2026-08-31 receipt in comment `f357b473-6456-4afd-bf92-089a7a22bf28` records all three measured criteria: LAN interactive login, continuously alive `main`, and Sting-produced signed PR [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808). ## 2026-10-04 — lab#2196 landed (R-C292, R-C11)

**Head merged:** `8e029ce51` (signed). It adds the adversarial-verify fix on top of `cafac1552`: a digest-field key must now start the line (after indentation and an optional YAML `- ` list marker) or follow `{`, `[` or `,`. Before this, keys that only end in a digest name were masked. Those are `hmac-digest:`, `secret-digest:`, `api-key-digest:`, `secret+digest:`, `password digest:`, `-digest:`, `--digest:` and `tool --digest:`, and all of them now block. The verify pass found and applied this fix. I committed it and pushed it with force-with-lease against `cafac1552` (a fast-forward).

**Tests (sting, origin/main merged with the PR head, nixpkgs python3.withPackages pytest+pyyaml, bounded):** I ran every unit test that references `global-git-hooks`: `test_agent_process_safety_audit.py`, `test_global_git_credential_protection.py` and `test_mcp_project_audit.py`. Result: **229 passed** in 78s. The commit-time agent process safety audit also passed (OK).

**Merge:** admin merge through the REST merge endpoint, because GraphQL was rate-limited. The merge was pinned to sha `8e029ce51`. Merge commit `6bd519351`, at 2026-10-04T10:31:15Z.

**Delivery:** not delivered yet. The hook reaches neo only through the batched Home Manager switch (R-C232).

**Accepted residual risks (need a new ruling to close):**
- A crafted value placed in an allowed context is not checked. Examples: `token: x/y@sha256:<hex>`, a secret in a digest field, or `foo, digest: sha256:<hex>` after a comma.
- The content scan still skips `.yaml`, `.yml` and `.json` files.
- `ref@<bare hex>` was never hex-checked, before or after this change.

**2026-10-04 06:30 EDT — R-C293 adversarial verify (lab#2202). Tests pass on sting. Not merged.**

Rulings: R-C293, R-C292, R-C11, OI-1002-Q16.

**What changed in #2202.** It is rebased onto #2196's pushed R-C292 head `cafac1552` and is now at signed head `147facb2f`.
- R-C293 allows a bare 64-hex value under `digest` and `image_digest`. So those two cases moved out of the R-C292 blocked-cases test.
- **Fake digest keys** such as `api_key_digest`. Decision: a key ending in `_digest` or `_sha256` is trusted only when nothing on the line looks like a secret name. The word list now also catches:
  - any word ending in `key` or `keys` (`master_key_sha256`, `masterKey_digest`)
  - `pass`, which covers passphrase and passcode
  - auth, bearer, session, cookie, salt, pepper, mnemonic, and `otp` as a standalone word
  - matching ignores case

  This also blocks public-key fingerprints such as `host_key_sha256:`. Blocking is the safe direction. Tests were added for each case.
- **Path spoofing** (a file named `provisioner/tenants/...` in another repo): no path is trusted. R-C293 adds no path rule. The existing skip for source-file extensions (.json, .yaml, .py) depends only on the extension, not the path. A new test puts a value under a non-digest key in scanned files at three spoofed paths, and each one blocks.
- **Residuals we accept**, which a check that reads one line of the diff at a time cannot close:
  - a secret-named parent key on a different line (`api_key:` and then `  digest: <hex>`)
  - deliberately misspelled names such as `s3cret_digest`

  Both are written up in the agent note in the PR.

**Validation on sting** (tinyland-heavy.slice, about 23 GiB MemAvailable), at `147facb2f`:
- `bazel test --nocache_test_results //tests:global_git_credential_protection`: 1 test passes.
- `nix-instantiate --parse` on the hook: OK.
- agent-notes index contract: OK.
- Afterwards: ran `bazel shutdown` and removed the verify worktree.

**Why it is not merged.** #2202 is stacked on #2196, and #2196 is not finished:
- The seat working on R-C292 has uncommitted changes in `lab-wt-r-c292` that fix a gap in #2196's pushed head.
- In that pushed head, the digest-field rule accepts a `-` or a space before the key. So `hmac-digest: sha256:<hex>` and `password digest: sha256:<hex>` are both masked and pass.
- Admin-merging #2202 now would do one of two things:
  - push R-C293 into a branch that seat is about to push to, or
  - if retargeted to main, land #2196 with that gap still open.

**Next steps:**
1. The R-C292 seat pushes its fix to #2196 and lands it.
2. Rebase #2202, retarget it to main, re-run the target on sting, then admin-merge (R-C11).

Merging is not delivery: the hook reaches neo only through the R-C232 batched switch. No Linear description was edited.

**Why a new path:** the R-C232 batched neo switch has to land by about 10-05, because GF's custody fill PR needs the R-C292/R-C293 hook allowance. Neo runs out of memory evaluating its own HM config (the R-C271 attempt died during eval), and PZM is blocked on its Nix DB repair (R-C287).

5. The operator picks the moment to activate (R-C232). The activation is receipted.

- prove the path at current main now;
- re-run it at the final main once #2196 (R-C292) and the R-C293 follow-up have merged;

## 2026-10-04 ~07:30Z: lab seat (neo), R-C286 (operator interview): attended repair of PZM's Nix DB

**R-C286:** repair PZM's corrupt `/nix/var/nix/db/db.sqlite` now, following the 2026-09-26 precedent. Steps:
1. Before anything else, state who is logged in on PZM, any tmux servers and any agent processes there (R-N11 service-lifecycle precondition).
2. Stop the named job `system/systems.determinate.nix-daemon` with `launchctl bootout`. This is permitted named-service lifecycle; it is not an agent, tmux or session surface.
3. Back up `db.sqlite` plus its `-wal` and `-shm` files next to the original with a dated suffix.
4. Rebuild the database: `sqlite3 .recover` (or dump and restore) into a new DB, then REINDEX. Run integrity_check; it must report ok.
5. Swap the new DB in.
6. Start the daemon again with `launchctl bootstrap` / `kickstart`.
7. Run `nix-store --verify` (without `--repair` unless needed), then the serialized GC to free `/nix`.

No reboot, no mount changes and no GF services. If integrity_check is not ok or the daemon fails to start, stop and report; the backup stays in place.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;

* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.

**2026-10-04: R-C293 lab#2202 has landed (R-C11 admin merge after local validation)**

- The verify pass on head `cde3234d8` passed with no must-block findings. It was signed (G) and rebased onto main `6bd519351`, which already includes #2196 / R-C292.
- **Sting validation:** I made a detached worktree of origin/main `6bd519351` and merged the PR head `cde3234d8` into it. Main is an ancestor of the head, and the merged tree is byte-identical to the head. I ran three test files: `test_global_git_credential_protection.py`, `test_agent_process_safety_audit.py` and `test_mcp_project_audit.py`. I used the nixpkgs `python3.withPackages [pytest pyyaml]` environment, bounded by `timeout`. Result: **233 passed in 100.58s**. The worktree and the temporary ref are removed.
- **Merge:** I used REST `PUT /pulls/2202/merge` with `merge_method=merge`, pinned to sha `cde3234d8855dfee058b67440c1a017f317f71bc`. Merge commit `505bccce7`, merged at 2026-10-04T10:53:06Z.
- Neo delivery goes with the batched switch (R-C232).

**Residuals the verifier recorded. None of these is fixed; each needs its own operator ruling:**
1. **Not on record before (PLAUSIBLE):** the secret-word line guard misses common abbreviations, so `sk_digest`, `pwd_sha256`, `cred_digest`, `jwt_sha256`, `priv_digest`, `access_sha256` and `wallet_sha256` all pass. A candidate widening is cred|pwd|priv|jwt plus standalone sk/psk. It was not applied, because narrowing an operator ruling needs its own ruling (the R-C284 precedent).
2. **Already on record from the #2196 landing:** an image ref under a secret key passes, for example `secret: ghcr.io/x/y@sha256:<hex>`.
3. **Not a regression:** hex that follows the mask with no `:`/`=` in front was never hex-checked.
4. **Outside R-C293's YAML/JSON scope:** `.tfvars` `plan_sha256 = "<hex>"` still blocks. Allowing it needs a new ruling.
5. **Held notes:** 3 of the 12 untracked 2026-10-04 notes still block (r-c255, r-c268, swb-land-15-11-clockseam-digest) because they quote `sha256:<hex>` in backticks. They need rewording into image-ref form or `digest: sha256:<hex>` field form before they land. This is not a hook defect.

## Active native-reset scope — 2026-10-02

Runtime source/current Bazel graph owns versioned release/reference facts and digests. Locked Nix/Bazel packages and consumers reconcile exact stamp, dirty state, targets, signatures/SBOM/provenance/support limits. No build.zig.zon/legacy manifest authority; npm retired. No tap/deploy/publication authorization inferred.

Acceptance: SC-11, RR-02, RR-03, RR-04. Source: [current contract](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/governance/repository-roles.md>). Checkpoint: NR+10h · executable readiness review (2026-10-03; exact time in core milestone). Severity: S1 adopted triage class, no staffed response commitment. Owner role: platform/delivery reviewer; preserve current assignee without inventing staff. Repository: oauth-mux runtime/source/evidence; site work belongs to separate [omux.xoxd.ai](<http://omux.xoxd.ai>) and consumes generated facts.

## Acceptance and evidence gate

Experimental, unshipped native reset. Install Omux, authorize sources once, and use ordinary application commands. Supported handoff preserves the same process and native session/history/tools/approvals with no routine prompt. No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

Authority: [active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>), [charter](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/charter.md>), [acceptance](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/user-stories.md>), [support gates](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/support-and-completeness.md>), [evidence](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/implementation/native-reset-evidence-2026-10-02.md>). Historical v0.1.15 and reviewed evidence retain their original claims; tracker completion cannot promote live support.

A reviewable completion attaches exact revision/artifact/platform/native/provider tuple, declared action receipt, predicates and limitations. Native/live/real-vault/installed gates remain unrun or blocked until their actual receipts exist. Dependencies are reconciled by links, not synthetic score.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Authority

`build.zig.zon` is the single human-edited version source and the Zig release graph owns target/product semantics. It deterministically emits and checks `release-manifest.json`. Consumers do not own independent versions or target lists.

## In scope

* GitHub release assets and checksums/signing inputs.
* Curl installer.
* Binary-only Homebrew formula.
* deb/rpm metadata.
* Nix/source consumption.
* Compatibility `oauth-mux` link beside primary `omux`.
* Service assets, SBOM/provenance, build ID, adapter protocol versions, and supported-platform declarations.

## Excluded

npm remains retired. Do not add `.pkg`, `.dmg`, AppImage, or another unratified lane. Windows managed broker is unsupported; any retained v0.1.15 artifact is compatibility history until the manifest explicitly removes it.

## Acceptance

One `build.zig.zon` version change causes the Zig graph to regenerate/check every supported consumer with no hand-edited drift. Clean-source and installed-artifact proofs agree on version, hashes, signatures, SBOM, provenance, and support matrix.

[TIN-3080](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-3080/relocate-egreg-emacs-daemon-honeysting-new-e)'s eGreg disposition follows its own completion record; historical storage incidents do not impose an unratified avoidance of `/srv/fast-local`.

Freeze the v0.2 process-level harness adapter contract and prove it with Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Control and redacted diagnostics use a versioned JSON-RPC subprocess boundary. There is no C ABI or shared-library SDK.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;
* local-only redacted events and stable schema versioning;
* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.
